what_it_is: The skeleton every IDP delivery shares: a document arrives, master data is pulled in, the document is matched against it, values are derived, the result is validated, a payload is built and sent. Targets differ in the payload, the auth, which master-data roles exist and how coding works - those live in profiles/, not here.

extraction.why_preferred: A custom engine extracts fields OUTSIDE the pretrained catalog and learns the customer's own layout, including line-item columns. rir_field_names can only reach the pretrained catalog, so any field the catalog lacks is left to a formula, a hook, or the operator.
extraction.constraint: Pretrained-SEEDED engine fields extract at catalog quality from day one; fields with pre_trained_field_id: null start COLD and learn from confirmed annotations in training_queues. So a custom engine is not a quality win on day one for catalog fields - it is a coverage win for everything else, plus a training path.
extraction.evidence: Tested, with a negative result worth recording: converting a queue from generic+rir_field_names to a custom engine with all mappable line-item columns seeded from table_column_* changed extraction NOT AT ALL on the test document - header fields identical, line items zero rows both ways. The zero rows were caused by a test PDF with no table geometry, not by the binding. So the case for a custom engine rests on COVERAGE (fields outside the pretrained catalog) and on having a training path - NOT on better extraction of fields the catalog already covers.
extraction.anti_claim: Do not sell a custom engine as fixing table extraction. If a document has no table structure, no engine will find one.

use_case.requirement: MUST be set deliberately whenever the schema has line-item columns

known_values.generic_ap: header-only - line-item columns extract NOTHING, silently

use_case.evidence: A/B measured: two engines with identical seeded tabular fields returned zero rows on generic_ap; patching one to coupa_line_level and re-importing the same invoice returned all three lines. This is the single setting that decides whether table extraction happens at all, and an engine created without it defaults to header-only.
use_case.failure_mode: silent - columns are created, look right, and stay empty on every document

column_binding.rule: A line-item column's rir_field_names must be the TABLE-COLUMN catalog field (table_column_description), not the header one (item_description). The multivalue itself carries rir_field_names: ['line_items'].
column_binding.why_it_matters: A column bound with the header vocabulary extracts nothing on the generic engine AND seeds nothing on conversion, so the failure survives the switch to a custom engine and looks like an engine problem.
column_binding.correction: This replaces an earlier claim in this file that the CONVERTER could not seed tabular columns. It can, and does, when the schema is authored correctly - proven by the skill's live-conversion ground-truth fixture. The P1 build's schema was mis-authored; the tool was right.

extraction.type_rule: The queue flip refuses when a schema datapoint's type differs from its engine field's, so the engine field must take the SCHEMA's type. pre_trained_field_id is independent of both name and type, so the seed is kept either way.

phases.goal: documents arrive from every channel the customer uses
decide: Which channels? email / manual upload / structured e-invoice feed. A structured feed needs its own import extension and changes validation (see intent A20).
Is there a national clearance regime in scope? (adds intent A19 and a compliance gate)
phases.verify: one document per channel reaches a processing queue with a populated document id

phases.goal: every field the recipe needs is extracted by the engine, not patched up downstream
decide: Custom engine (preferred) or generic + rir_field_names? Custom whenever the schema has fields outside the pretrained catalog - which in practice is every implementation with target-specific coding, tax or reference fields.
Which fields seed from the pretrained catalog and which start cold? Seeded fields work immediately; cold fields need a training corpus, so say who confirms documents and how many.
greenfield (new queue born engine-bound) or convert (existing generic queue)? Converting rewrites the schema: rir_field_names cleared, ui_configuration normalised to captured/enabled.
Is the schema shared by more than one queue? Conversion refuses - copy the schema first.
phases.verify: on 20 real documents, every engine-extracted field the export contract needs is populated, INCLUDING line-item columns - table extraction is the thing catalog-only binding gets wrong
phases.snapshot: always pass --snapshot-dir; the snapshot is the revert path

phases.goal: every collection matching depends on is present and fresh
decide: Import mechanism: hosted scheduled import vs custom function vs file drop. Measured across 6 implementations: all three occur; the hosted import is the least code.
Refresh cadence per role — PO lines usually need the highest.
phases.verify: each role's collection returns a non-zero row count, and a spot-checked key resolves
phases.gap: no part exists for import scheduling; build from mdh-reference

phases.goal: each document lands in the queue whose rules and coding apply to it
decide: Route by country, legal entity, or document type? This choice fixes queue_axis and is expensive to change later.
Routing mechanism: native rule change_queue vs a sorting store-extension. Measured: both occur; a store extension holds routing rules for 3 of 6 implementations.
phases.verify: 20 real documents land in the expected queue; zero in the inbox after processing

phases.goal: supplier, buying entity and PO resolve, or the document is explicitly marked unmatched
decide: Is matching gated per country? Measured: 71% of match configs carry an action_condition. If yes, the gate is part of every intent here.
Fuzzy fallback: yes/no per role. A cascade (exact -> fuzzy) was used for 44% of configs.
Memorised-alias loop: does operator confirmation feed back into matching? (adds a write-back part and a union query)
Does validation compare the service period against the PO's dates? If yes, the PO-line import must carry PO start/end dates - a collection-shape decision, not a rule decision.
phases.verify: match rate on 20 real documents above the agreed threshold, and every no-match visibly flagged

requires.preflight: Atlas search index exists on every collection a fuzzy query names

phases.goal: values the target needs, and values validation needs, are computed
decide: Normalise identifiers before matching (VAT ids, PO references, payment terms)? Strongly recommended: it collapses per-variant validation rules.
Which coding dimensions does the target require, and do segments resolve as a chain?
phases.verify: for 20 documents, every derived field the export contract requires is populated

phases.goal: a non-PO invoice carries complete, valid coding
decide: Coding source: matched from master data, memorised from operator behaviour, or manual?
Segment chain order — one segment's match may feed the next's lookup.
phases.verify: a non-PO document exports with every required segment populated; a deliberately incomplete one is blocked

phases.goal: no document leaves with data the target will reject or a human would not sign
decide: Tolerance for totals reconciliation: exact or absolute epsilon? Both occur; epsilon is kinder to rounding.
Which failures block versus warn? Measured split on one implementation: 92 blocking, 100 messaging.
Are diagnostics surfaced to operators as tags? (couples intent B1 to the formulas that compute them)
Declare thresholds as named constants at the top of each condition (the baseline's style) rather than inlining numbers.
phases.verify: each gating intent fires on a hand-built failing document and passes a clean one

phases.goal: the target accepts the payload and its response is recorded
decide: Packaging: single request-processor hook (preferred for new work) vs a per-call chain (widely deployed, fully valid). A chain with a mid-chain formula dependency CANNOT collapse into one hook — formulas evaluate only after a hook completes.
How many outbound legs? Measured: payload, attachment, backlink, status submit — 1 to 4 legs.
Are later legs gated on an earlier response?
phases.verify: one real document is accepted by the target, its identifier is written back, and a forced failure surfaces as a readable error

derivation.constraint: must run BEFORE matching consumes it

matching.note: the mined tree imports this role but never matches it

hook_chain.derivation_note: NOT hand-authored. Derived from the field-flow graph: 29 fields flow matching->formula, 64 formula->rule, 11 through all three. An edge exists wherever a downstream mechanism reads a field an upstream one writes.

annotation_content.initialize|started|up.why_here: routing needs the buying entity before queue-specific logic applies
matching consumes normalised identifiers; running after matching reads empty
supplier and PO must resolve before anything derived from them
gated on entity and country resolved above; internally chained

validation.why_here: 48% of gates read formula-derived values; all must run after derivation
surfaces the flags computed in the flag stage

platform_contract._why: Facts that cost a failed call each during the P1 build. None is discoverable from the intent catalogues or the reference packs, and every one of them is the kind of thing a recipe exists to carry forward.
rules: A multi-line trigger_condition MUST be wrapped in parentheses - Python cannot continue an expression across lines. The baseline's ( ... ) wrapper is functional, not house style. 7 of 20 rules failed on this and the error does not name the failing rule.
Each action needs a client-supplied UUID `id`; the server does not generate one.
payload.schema_id anchors a message to a field in the UI.
Rules bind through `queues` (an array of URLs), not a single `queue`.
Declare thresholds as named constants at the top of the condition (baseline style).
matching: EVERY field an MDH config writes must be type: enum - additional_mappings targets included. One bad target fails the whole config and it writes nothing at all.
A fuzzy stage needs a search index or it returns zero rows SILENTLY.
A private Store extension cannot be POSTed (config.url is null and POST demands one). Duplicate an existing hook and PATCH its settings; check for hook_templates first.
formulas: Formula fields cap at 2000 characters. Anything larger - notably a target payload - belongs in a template hook. This is WHY intent E1 is realized_by custom_format_template.
A formula cannot read page text directly; a part must park it in a field first, after which a formula CAN search it.
export_pipeline: response_handlers use target_type + target_key + value, and the value is a context-path shorthand like {"response.body": {"$jmespath": "id"}}. Verify against the deployed engine's own model - the engine version is FROZEN AT CREATION and the reference may document a different build.
evaluate entries are {name, condition}, not bare condition dicts.

content_type MUST be "json" when the body arrives via the .@ auto-fetch: the fetch calls response.json() for an application/json document, so the body is a parsed DICT. With content_type omitted the engine form-encodes it under a JSON header and the target answers 500.
get_content raises KeyError: 0 on an empty result instead of skipping - gate every optional get_content stage on the source existing.
Hook retries amplify one failure into many log entries. Sort newest-first and confirm the latest entry is not a success before debugging the errors above it.
platform: token_owner must be a user in the SAME organization.
Data Storage find takes `query`, not `filter`, and returns a bare array at .result.
content/operations does not fire hooks by design, so a hand-injected line item is never matched - it cannot be used to test the matched-line path.
A part registered only on annotation_content.initialize cannot be verified by a soft re-fire; budget a re-upload.
platform_contract.parts_library_defect: A seam used as an ATTRIBUTE NAME must be filled with a bare identifier. capture-page-text-to-field writes t.field.«first_page_field», so filling with "page_text" yields t.field."page_text" -> SyntaxError. part.json calls the param "type": "string", which invites the wrong fill.
extraction_engines: engine.settings.use_case gates line-item extraction; omitting it yields a header-only engine that silently extracts no rows. Set it explicitly for any line-item schema.
Line-item columns bind to table_column_* rir names; the multivalue binds to ['line_items']. Header vocabulary (item_*) on a column extracts nothing and seeds nothing.
The queue flip compares schema datapoint type to engine field type and 400s on a mismatch; the engine field should take the schema's type and keep its seed.
pre_trained_field_id is independent of the engine field's name and type - no schema rename is needed to seed a differently-named field.

A custom engine is behaviour-neutral for catalog header fields; its value is coverage of non-catalog fields plus a training path. It does not improve extraction of fields the catalog already covers, and it cannot find a table that is not in the document.

gaps: Function-code intents are NOT in this recipe. One profiled implementation keeps 97% of its logic in Python; this recipe would describe almost none of it.
No parts exist yet for: master-data import scheduling, the memorised-alias write-back loop, the response-extractor chain.
Automation outcome is absent by design - no evidence band is claimed for this shape.
n=1. Every 'measured' figure here comes from one implementation unless it says otherwise.

provenance.cluster_basis: shape records over local prd2 pulls, deduplicated (second pulls of one customer and copies of a baseline counted once); cluster is ap_invoice x coupa x https_out
provenance.honest_statement: The CLUSTER is 7 implementations - that is what justifies publishing this shape at all. The INTENTS were extracted from 1 implementation and cross-checked against 1 hand-authored baseline, which added 17 and withdrew 0. Do not read 54 intents as the consensus of 7 trees; the other 5 have been clustered, not mined.
provenance.next: extract intents from the remaining 5 cluster members; expect the count to keep rising - the baseline alone added 17
provenance.validation: 39/49 of the baseline's rules covered by mined intents, 17 added, 0 withdrawn
provenance.built_end_to_end: one worked recipe from a single-country SOW: 31 objects, 8 phases, invoices created in a live target with line-level tax and tags
provenance.scope: The SPINE is the shape of every IDP delivery and is not tied to one target. The counts below describe the cluster the intents were mined from; a new target needs a PROFILE, not a new recipe.
